title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 5th District
area: North and central Louisiana, including the Delta and Avoyelles, Rapides and Ouachita parishes.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map. This is an open seat: incumbent Julia Letlow (R) did not seek re-election here, running instead for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Michael Echols
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Representative, District 14 (Chairman, House Republican Delegation)

summary.text: Michael Echols is a Louisiana State Representative for District 14, businessman and developer from Monroe who chairs the House Republican Delegation. He leads Echo Development, which has revitalized historic properties in North Louisiana, and hosts a radio show, "Echols at 8." He is running for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District on public safety, energy and jobs, and reducing federal spending.

background.text: Leads Echo Development, a real-estate development company that has revitalized historic properties across North Louisiana, including The Hotel Monroe.
Serves as Louisiana State Representative for District 14 and as Chairman of the House Republican Delegation.

priorities.text: Says Washington has failed on public safety and pledges to use federal tools to put more officers on the street and target repeat violent offenders.
priorities.quote: Washington has failed on public safety. I'll use federal tools to put more officers on the street, support law enforcement, and go after repeat violent offenders. Safe communities come first.

priorities.text: Wants to cut regulation and expand energy production, including oil and gas and data infrastructure along the I-20 corridor.
priorities.quote: Cut red tape, unleash energy, and bring jobs back home. From oil and gas to new data infrastructure along I-20, we should be leading—not watching opportunity leave.

priorities.text: Pledges to rein in federal spending, saying Washington "spends too much, wastes too much, and puts Americans last."

summary.text: Oscar Dantzler, also known as Omar, is a Republican candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District.

Austin Magee is a small-business owner and builder running as a Republican candidate for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District, campaigning as a political outsider on political reform and fiscal responsibility.

background.text: Works as a blue-collar small business owner and builder; has no previous political experience.
background.quote: I want to prove that an ordinary person with no previous political experience can do the job with common sense and integrity.

priorities.text: Wants to "reform politics itself," including banning congressional stock trading, passing a term-limits amendment, and limiting lobbying.
Calls for fiscal responsibility, saying the country cannot let politicians bankrupt it.
Wants federal action to regulate AI, saying it should never be given power to decide life or death.

positions.summary: Describes himself as "pro life" in his survey response.
Says he is passionate about protecting constitutional rights, especially the first and second amendments.
Says he supports law enforcement, the military and veterans.

candidates.name: Dan McKay
candidates.currentRole: Attorney; city attorney for Bunkie, Hessmer and Evergreen, Louisiana

summary.text: Dan McKay is an attorney from Avoyelles Parish who has practiced law for over 45 years, including as a public defender, assistant district attorney, and city attorney for several central Louisiana towns. He is a U.S. Army veteran running as the Democratic candidate for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District on protecting rural hospitals, democratic institutions, and reproductive healthcare decisions.

background.text: U.S. Army veteran with two years overseas service; graduate of the LSU Law Center.
Maintained a general law practice in Avoyelles Parish for over 45 years, including 15 years as a public defender and more than 11 years as an assistant district attorney.
Has served as city attorney for Bunkie (12 years), Hessmer (24 years) and Evergreen (18 years).

priorities.text: Warns that about 20 rural hospitals in the 5th District are under threat of closing due to Medicaid cuts in the 2026 federal budget law.
Says healthcare should be viewed as a human right, and that a woman's healthcare decisions should be made between her and her medical professionals.
priorities.quote: Women's healthcare should be a matter of decision-making between a woman and her medical professionals.

priorities.text: Says the principles of democracy, including separation of church and state, free elections, rule of law, and a free press, are under attack and must be protected.

positions.summary: Says decisions about women's healthcare should be made between a woman and her medical professionals.
positions.quote: Women's healthcare should be a matter of decision-making between a woman and her medical professionals.

positions.summary: Says healthcare should be viewed as a human right and opposes Medicaid cuts that threaten rural hospitals in the district.
Says working people are "starved financially and paid sparsely while repeated tax cuts favor only the most wealthy."

researchNotes: This is a crowded open-seat race (9 candidates). Michael Echols, Austin Magee and Dan McKay completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. Misti Cordell (the best-funded Republican after Echols), Oscar Dantzler, Patricia Moore and Antonio Wilson had no campaign website, survey response, or other public statements found beyond their names and party on the ballot. Gabe Firment and Stewart Cathey are current Louisiana state legislators but did not complete the survey or have an accessible campaign site with issue positions; only their current office is documented here.
